record.title: Routines /trigger 1/min rate limit is a non-atomic check-then-set and may be bypassable with parallel requests
record.description: Mechanism verified from source and local simulation, but rejected as a standalone record: the check-then-set is real (L209 get, L211 60s check, L214 probe await widening the window, L223 put; no lock/CAS/transaction anywhere in the file, and KV has no atomic CAS), and a local simulation of that exact interleaving returns [202,202] for two parallel triggers vs [202,429] sequentially. However it adds no independent impact: /trigger is already unauthenticated (unlike token-gated POST /api/routines), so anyone can already trigger once a minute, and a race only yields a few extra pending entries per minute in the same abuse class — /trigger only wakes QwenPaw and records a PENDING prompt, it executes nothing. Token-gating /trigger (the fix for the confirmed unauthenticated-trigger finding) makes the race moot for attackers. Fold this as a note under that confirmed finding, not a separate record.

trace.what: POST /trigger handler; no auth/token check, unlike POST /api/routines at L186-191 which requires X-Routine-Token
const last = await env.STATUS.get('routines:last-trigger-at') — read of the rate-limit timestamp
if (last && now - Number(last) < TRIGGER_MIN_GAP_MS) return 429 — check, TRIGGER_MIN_GAP_MS=60000 at L35
const probe = await probeQwenPaw(env) — network await between check and write, widening the interleave window (probe timeout up to 20000ms)
await env.STATUS.put('routines:last-trigger-at', String(now)) — write, separate KV op after L222 pending-entry put; no lock, CAS, transaction or Durable Object anywhere (grep finds no such primitive)

evidence.output: 35:const TRIGGER_MIN_GAP_MS = 60_000; 209:const last = await env.STATUS.get("routines:last-trigger-at"); 211:if (last && now - Number(last) < TRIGGER_MIN_GAP_MS) { 222:await env.STATUS.put(PENDING_PREFIX + id, JSON.stringify(entry)); 223:await env.STATUS.put("routines:last-trigger-at", String(now)); — no DurableObject/transaction/lock/mutex/atomic/CAS hits

evidence.command: node /tmp/race-sim.js (local simulation of L209-223 logic with async KV mock + 50ms probe await; no production requests fired)
evidence.output: sequential: [202,429] (expect [202,429]); parallel 2: [202,202] (expect [202,202] if race is real)
POST /api/routines requires ROUTINE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN / X-Routine-Token (503 fail-closed if unset, 401 on mismatch); POST /trigger at L206 has no such check before the L209 read

record.conditions: Race is real as a mechanism: concurrent Workers isolates can both await the L209 get before either reaches the L223 put, and the L214 probe await makes the window seconds-wide, not a single tick. Cloudflare KV is eventually consistent across edge locations, which widens rather than narrows the race (a stale read in another colo also passes the check); the file itself makes no strong-consistency claim. Local simulation proves the interleaving logic only — it does not prove a production parallel burst succeeds, and no parallel production requests were fired per task constraints.
record.remediation: Token-gate POST /trigger exactly like POST /api/routines (require X-Routine-Token matching ROUTINE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, fail closed 503 when unset) — this is the correct fix for the abuse class and makes the race moot for unauthenticated callers. Note token-gating alone does not make the check atomic; if strict 1/min atomicity is ever required, move the check-and-set into a Durable Object (single-threaded, sequential execution), since KV offers no CAS. A Durable Object solely for this soft 1/min limit is disproportionate — the limit guards wake/probe volume, not a security boundary.
record.reason: Rejected as a standalone record, not because the race is false — the non-atomic read-check-write and its interleave window are verified. Rejected because it has no independent impact: the confirmed unauthenticated-trigger finding already lets anyone trigger once a minute, the race only adds a few extra PENDING entries per minute in the same abuse class, /trigger executes nothing, and the confirmed finding's token-gating fix moots it. Keeping it standalone would double-count one abuse class. Fold it as a note under the confirmed unauthenticated-trigger finding.
